title: Find earlier printed evidence for words the Oxford English Dictionary has appealed on
done_when: Every appealed word and sense has the year of the earliest printed use that two AIs of different vendors found on an open scan and agree on, and whether that year is earlier than the dictionary's, with the source, the date and page, the quotation and the search that found it kept as evidence for a reader to open the scan; an earlier use found later, read on its page, supersedes an accepted answer through a challenge.

word/*.brief: Word {n}: {word.word}, {word.pos}, in the sense: {word.sense}. The Oxford English Dictionary asked the public for earlier evidence of this word in this sense on its OED Appeals pages, which ran from 2012 to 2018 and are kept today by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine; when it asked, the earliest evidence in its entry was {word.then_date}: {word.then_source}. Find the earliest printed use of the word in this sense that can be read on an open scan: the Internet Archive, HathiTrust in full view, Chronicling America at the Library of Congress, Google Books in full view, Trove at the National Library of Australia, Papers Past at the National Library of New Zealand, or another library's scan that opens without a login; read the words on the page image or in its full text. A quotation website, a dictionary, an encyclopedia, a snippet view that hides the page, or a database behind a login is not evidence, though any of them may point to a scan. The use counts only in the sense above: an earlier use of the same spelling in another sense does not. Return year, a whole number: the year of the earliest use found this way, taken from the issue's masthead or dateline for a newspaper or a periodical and from the title page for a book, a reprint dated by the reprint unless the scan is of the original edition; when nothing earlier than the dictionary's date is found, year is the dictionary's year, {word.then_year}. Return found_earlier, yes when year is less than {word.then_year}, and no otherwise, including when the earliest use found falls in the same year as the dictionary's. Then return source, the newspaper, periodical or book, with its author or editor where there is one; place, the date of the issue or the edition and the page or column; quotation, the words on the page in which the word appears, at most sixty words, copied as they stand; where_seen, the archive and the identifier or title of the scan, named in words; how_found, the search that led to it, in a sentence; and notes, anything uncertain, including a hit that may be a misreading in the scan's text layer. When nothing earlier is found, source, place, quotation and where_seen each give the word none and how_found says what was searched. Every field is plain text with no links; sources are named by title.
